transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-09-25
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood PM), Samir (Vectorly Head ML), Rina (Vectorly Platform Eng), Leo (Vectorly CTO - joined briefly)

Summary (auto): Quick Optimize console walkthrough showing how to generate quantization profiles, run INT8/FP8 sensitivity tests, and interpret the fidelity-vs-latency heatmap. Agreed to run an initial sandbox benchmark using Vectorly's moderation prompts and then expand to their customer-facing low-latency route.

00:00:05 Maya: hey everyone thanks for taking the time today, we'll run through the Optimize console and the quant profiles, um Diego is gonna do the hands-on stuff and Priya will jump in for the rollout Qs
00:00:14 Samir: thanks Maya, excited. Our big thing — we ship a realtime classification endpoint so p95 latency needs to be sub 120 ms, we also need to keep false positives under 1.5% on the moderation set
00:00:29 Diego: got it, that p95 SLO is useful; I'll show the profiling workflow, how we collect sequence length distributions then recommend an INT8 or FP8 profile, and importantly the fallback waterfall if quality regresses
00:00:45 Rina: quick housekeeping — we care about private data, so we'll want VPC and KMS keys in pilot, is that supported in the sandbox?
00:00:55 Maya: sandbox supports a VPC-like isolation and we can stage KMS; Diego will include the security doc link after the meeting, it's in the deck we shared — link: https://redwood.example/sandbox-sec
00:01:07 Priya: also worth noting Optimize has a sensitivity scorer that ranks prompts by quality delta when you change precision, this helps pick canary prompts

00:02:30 Diego: OK jumping into the console, um can everyone see my screen, I have the Vectorly sandbox plan here, you can see the Profile tab, we start by uploading a prompt corpus, then run a warmup so the KV cache — sometimes transcribed as K V cash — is populated and the runtime gets stable
00:02:52 Samir: the corpus we'll send is about 10k real requests, most are short 20-40 tokens but we have a tail to 512 tokens for escalations
00:03:05 Diego: perfect, that's the kind of distribution we need. Alright I'm going to trigger the profiling job in the console — it runs microbenchmarks across batch sizes and step lengths and then produces a heatmap: fidelity on Y axis, latency delta on X axis
00:03:32 Rina: can you run both INT8 and FP8 in the same job? We want a side-by-side comparison not two separate reports
00:03:39 Diego: yes you can. We spin up two quant buckets and run the same set; Optimize outputs a combined diff report and a recommended precision per route. It also calculates expected cost per 1M tokens for each profile
00:04:01 Priya: small caveat — FP8 sometimes shows better latency for small batches on newer kernels, but it's workload dependent; the tool flags when FP8 is faster vs when INT8 compresses more for throughput-heavy flows
00:04:23 Samir: when you say 'recommended precision per route' does that mean we can have hybrid: INT8 for the low-importance internal enrichment route and FP8 for the critical moderation route?
00:04:31 Maya: exactly, you can configure per-route precision and have automatic fallback to a higher-fidelity profile if a quality check fails
00:04:43 Diego: right, think of it as a precision policy chain: preferred -> conservative -> safety. If the canary prompts exceed the allowed regression threshold we failover automatically and send an alert to the Console and to Slack
00:05:00 Samir: nice, can we customize the regression threshold? we want 0.5% drop detection on precision-sensitive prompts, 2% on others
00:05:08 Priya: yes thresholds are configurable per route and per prompt set. The console stores historical fidelity metrics so you can set percentiles for rolling windows
00:05:20 Leo (brief): just curious, how disruptive is the migration, do you need model retraining?
00:05:26 Diego: no retraining; quant is applied at serving time. The risk is quant-induced quality degradation which we detect via the sensitivity tests and human-in-the-loop review if needed
00:05:40 Rina: what about mixed precision on a single request? say we have a short prompt then a long context, do you re-evaluate mid-stream?
00:05:49 Diego: good question — runtime supports on-the-fly policy routing but not mid-token precision switching; we pick the profile per request based on metadata (route id, sequence length, customer tier) and use KV cache for efficient continuation
00:06:05 Samir: any gotchas on latency numbers? our infra folks worry about cold-starts and autoscaling spikes
00:06:12 Diego: the profiler reports steady-state and cold-starts. For cold-starts, FP8 warms slightly slower on some kernels because of kernel selection overhead; but warm throughput often favors FP8 on newer hardware. We show p50/p95/p99 in the report
00:06:30 Maya: Diego will attach an example heatmap from a recent customer so you can see the buckets and recommended cutoffs — it's in the follow-up artifacts
00:06:42 Samir: ok let's talk fidelity — how are regressions measured? Is it BLEU? we need a metric that matches our moderation KPIs
00:06:50 Priya: by default we compute a suite of metrics: token-level perplexity, ROC AUC for classification-like tasks, and also a customizable scorer; you can plug in your own evaluation script to compute false-positive rate or moderation accuracy
00:07:05 Rina: perfect, we'll supply our scorer that maps to false positive rate
00:07:12 Diego: I'm starting the run now, you'll see a job id. It runs sample generation and then the sensitivity delta table, there might be noise so we bootstrap with multiple seeds and produce confidence intervals
00:07:35 [screen changes, console shows job: qprofile-vecly-091]
00:07:40 Diego: job kicked off. While that runs, a quick demo of the fallback policy editor — you can set this: if canary delta > 0.5% revert within 5 minutes and route traffic to Dedicated pool A, or fallback to hosted high-fidelity variant. You can also attach a webhook for your audit logs
00:08:02 Rina: Dedicated pool A — you mean reserved capacity? pricing-wise, can you give us an estimate for bursts for our traffic shape?
00:08:12 Maya: we'll send a burst pricing spreadsheet. For Vectorly's expected p95 and token volume, Dedicated burst for peak hours is often cheaper than falling back to pure FP8 on hosted tiers — we'll quantify in the follow-up
00:08:25 Samir: speaking of cost, do you show per-token cost delta on the heatmap? We want to balance cost vs latency vs quality
00:08:31 Diego: yes cost per million tokens is computed assuming your chosen hardware profile. It's an output column in the diff report so you can filter by latency percentile and cost impact simultaneously
00:08:45 Samir: good. also curious about auditability — we need immutable records of which profile served each request for compliance
00:08:52 Priya: Console logs per-request metadata including profile id, model version, and key fingerprint. Those are exportable to S3 and can be fed to your SIEM. We'll include sample log schema in the security doc
00:09:05 Rina: that helps. any differences in telemetry for Dedicated vs Hosted? we run in our own VPC for pilot
00:09:12 Maya: telemetry is the same; for Private/VPC there is an agent that ships logs to your collectors. The Control plane still provides the Optimize UI and analytics unless you choose fully air-gapped
00:09:25 Leo: joining back — is the pilot realistic to run for two weeks? we need to see sustained p95 < 120ms under production-like load
00:09:33 Diego: yes two weeks is fine, we recommend a 14-day pilot with initial canary then 7 days of ramped traffic; we'll instrument p95 and quality metrics and produce a pilot report
00:09:45 Samir: what's the recommended canary percentage?
00:09:48 Priya: typically 1-5% for high-risk routes; you can run higher for non-critical routes to gather quicker stats
00:09:56 Rina: during pilot, if FP8 looks better on latency but worse on our false positive, do you support hybrid fallbacks per-customer? we have tiered customers
00:10:05 Diego: yes per-tenant routing is supported. You can pin enterprise customers to higher fidelity while using aggressive profiles on low-tier traffic to cut costs
00:10:15 Samir: the profiler finished?
00:10:18 Diego: yes results are in. I'll share the screen — here's the heatmap: X axis is % latency change vs baseline fp32, Y axis is quality delta (lower is worse), color reflects cost change. For your moderation set, INT8 shows a 1.8% quality regression at p95 but reduces cost by 35%, FP8 shows 0.6% regression and 20% cost saving with slightly better p95 on this kernel
00:10:50 Rina: ok can you highlight per-route recs?
00:10:53 Diego: Route A (real-time moderation): recommend FP8 preferred, INT8 is conservative fallback only for non-peak windows. Route B (enrichment batch): recommend INT8 with aggressive batching. Route C (escalation long context): prefer high-fidelity fp32 or hosted high-fidelity variant due to long-tail token counts
00:11:12 Samir: that split makes sense. How do we implement the switch during a live rollout?
00:11:18 Diego: in Console: create policy, attach routes, set canary and thresholds, choose fallback targets. We also provide SDK flags so you can override per-request from your app if you detect an edge-case
00:11:30 Maya: I'll also note there's an audit log and a rollback button in the UI; if a canary triggers we can auto-rollback and notify the owners
00:11:40 Rina: what about model variants? we're concerned about vendor lock if we pin specific kernels
00:11:46 Priya: Optimize suggests model variants that are functionally equivalent; we surface compatibility. Fallback chain can include same-arch model with higher precision, or a different vendor's compatible checkpoint if you license it
00:12:02 Samir: you mentioned earlier that FP8 sometimes runs faster on newer kernels — is that something we should watch for production drift
00:12:08 Diego: yes kernel upgrades or new hardware can shift the trade-offs; Console flags when heatmap deltas change significantly after infra updates, and we recommend re-profiling on new runtime releases
00:12:22 Rina: any headroom for autoscaling? on spikes we need temporary extra nodes; can the fallback go to a burst Dedicated pool automatically
00:12:30 Diego: yes you can configure autoscaling policy that, on saturation, routes specific traffic to Dedicated burst capacity or to a hosted fallback; we can set a throttle so cost doesn't explode
00:12:45 Samir: one more technical — how deterministic are the quant profiles across seeds? we can't have wildly different quality by run
00:12:52 Diego: we bootstrap across seeds and report confidence intervals; if variance is high we mark the profile as "unstable" and recommend longer sampling or conservative defaults
00:13:05 Maya: ok let's capture next steps — Diego will provision sandbox and API keys; Samir will send the 10k prompt corpus and the custom scorer; Maya will send security and pricing; follow-up meeting in ~10 days to review results
00:13:18 Samir: sounds good, appreciate the walkthrough
00:13:25 Leo: thanks all, excited to see the pilot numbers
00:13:30 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll send notes and artifacts; Diego will share the heatmap screenshot and the qprofile job id in the CRM next

[End of recording — remaining ~58 minutes was Q&A and some live console fiddling not fully captured by the auto transcript due to screen share focus and some crosstalk. Partial snippets below]

00:15:00 Speaker 2: (mumbled) — the batching knob seems to prefer three tokens but our median is 28...
00:17:14 Diego: yeah the autosizer suggests a batch size distribution, you can pin to a manual batch size if your latencies are sensitive
00:22:40 Rina: (aside) their console labels are sometimes weird, e.g., 'precision lane' got transcribed as 'precision lanee' in our notes
00:28:12 Samir: hypothetically, if we had to delay pilot because of procurement, what's necessary to keep momentum
00:28:20 Maya: short answer: we can do a lower-friction 'analysis-only' run where we profile offline with your dataset and give a report without provisioning Dedicated pools, that keeps the momentum and gives a decision memo for procurement
00:33:01 Diego: also flagging risk: INT8 sensitivity for classification can spike on edge-case prompts; we recommended a fuzz-testing pass to detect brittle cases
00:40:10 Priya: pricing note — per-route reserved commits for Dedicated reduce unit price significantly; we'll include examples in the pricing spreadsheet
00:49:50 Samir: rough ask — can you show us a sample canary report that includes false positive delta rather than just perplexity?
00:49:58 Diego: yes we'll include a canary report template; send your scorer and we'll plug it into the sandbox run
00:58:03 Rina: can you export the full report to CSV? our analysts prefer that
00:58:10 Diego: yes CSV and JSON exports available, with per-prompt diffs and confidence intervals
